say: This is Minecraft. Except I built it.
From scratch. No game engine. No Mojang. Just me and C plus plus, a language that hates me personally. [boom]
Here's how it started.
Day one. The goal: one cube, on the screen. That's it.
Sounds easy. It is not. [scratch]
To draw anything, you have to talk to the graphics card. I picked a language for that called Vulkan.
In Vulkan, just saying hello takes about a thousand lines of code.
So after a full day of yelling at my laptop: behold. A cube. [boom]
It's red, it's green, it's checkered. It looks like a Rubik's cube that gave up on life.
I have never been prouder of anything. [ding]
But Minecraft isn't one cube. It's millions.
So I made a cube, out of cubes. [boom]
Every block has six faces. But a face pressed against another block can never be seen, so I just don't draw it.
Free performance. The best kind of performance. [boom]
Minecraft cuts its world into chunks. Mine are thirty-two blocks wide, tall and deep.
This one has three thousand, four hundred and fifteen faces.
Minecraft shows hundreds of these at once. Do the math. Actually, don't. [scratch]
So, a trick. If two faces next to each other look the same, glue them into one big face.
Two hundred and seventy-five. Same chunk. Twelve times fewer faces. [boom]
Is that cheating? Yes. Am I going to stop? No. [boom]
Next time: making it actually look like Minecraft. Follow, or the cube gets it. [scratch]
